input.rationale: Registered the successor execution for the strongest remaining boundary: the harness adds a split_configurations case where a three-voter committed configuration is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted and made three voters again, the leader is partitioned from the other two in both directions and taken down, only it is restarted (with a fresh instance beside it), and both sides then run. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled both sides elected leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums — the restarted side on a one-voter reconstruction, the other two on the committed three-voter configuration — both committed an entry, and neither side held the other's entry; with the flag disabled only the two-peer side led and the restarted side refused with "node is not the leader".

scope.description: Whether a reconstruction-governed leader and the peers of the committed configuration can both lead and commit when a partition separates them. Twenty-one in-process cases: the nineteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a split_configurations case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, the leader is disconnected from the other two in both directions and stopped, only it is restarted together with a fresh empty instance, and both sides are left to elect and commit.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the partition is made with the transport's own Disconnect on both sides, and the fresh instance is connected only to the restarted leader.

The restarted leader's reconstruction is the single-voter configuration recorded by its own snapshot while the configuration entry in its log names three voters; the two partitioned peers keep the committed configuration.
Each side is given up to 800 ms to elect, then both are asked to commit one uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, and each side's log store is searched for the other side's entry afterwards.
No instance is restarted after the partition, and no other membership change is issued on the second side.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, healing of the partition, multiple sequential client changes, and any claim about what the cluster would do if the partition were repaired.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back, applies ten more entries and reads the last configuration entry into a split_inputs CA_EVENT. It disconnects the leader from both peers in both directions with the transport's Disconnect, stops the leader, restarts it over its own stores with the case flag, starts one fresh empty instance (own stores and FSM) connected only to it, and waits for it to lead. It then issues AddVoter for the fresh instance, waits for a leader among the two partitioned peers, records both sides' terms and reconstructed voter counts, has both sides commit a uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, waits, searches each side's log store for the other side's entry, and emits a split_result CA_EVENT with both sides' leadership, terms, voter counts, commit outcomes, whether each side holds its own and the other's entry, the derived cross_entries_seen and whether both sides lead and in the same term.
experiment.responsibility: Election quorums and leader commitments are computed from each node's own reconstructed configuration, so whether two quorums overlap is decided by that configuration rather than by the committed one.

comparisons.description: Partition case with the flag enabled: a cluster is not expected to have a leader on the restarted side and a leader among the peers of the committed configuration at the same time.
Partition case with the flag enabled: two leaders are not expected to hold the same term.
Partition case with the flag enabled: an entry committed on one side is expected to be visible to the other side's store, so both committed entries should be found across the two sides.
Control: with the flag disabled the restarted side cannot lead with only one of the committed configuration's three voters reachable, so only the other side leads.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: four in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities, pairing RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled within two single-voter committed shapes. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, optionally snapshots and then commits RemoveServer for the non-leader peer, reads the configuration entry and tracked commit index from the surviving instance's own log store, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same log, stable and snapshot stores plus a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In both shapes the committed configuration after the setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration (1 voter) with no snapshot, or a snapshot taken before a committed RemoveServer that leaves 1 voter while the snapshot metadata still holds 2.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms) and the flag-disabled control runs the identical setup for each shape.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

basis.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands through the elected leader, and for the second shape calls leader.Snapshot() followed by leader.RemoveServer(non-leader ID) plus 10 more applies. Before the restart it reads, from the surviving instance's own stores, the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list) together with the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it then shuts down every instance and restarts the survivor with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote. Each emitted CA_EVENT JSON line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity, plus raw operands (latest_config_index, log_config_index, snapshot_config_index and the server lists), the instance's own configuration, the public GetConfiguration view, last_applied, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix, election attempts and became_leader over the 3000 ms window.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; no component outside Raft is required to repair it.

scope.description: Whether ordinary replication from a healthy leader repairs a restarted follower's reconstructed configuration, and whether a later configuration entry does. Eleven in-process cases: the nine previously exercised restart shapes plus a follower_in_live_cluster case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-peer cluster removes one peer while keeping three entries of history, the remaining follower is stopped and restarted while the leader keeps leading and replicating, the follower is observed after 400 ms, and the leader then re-adds the removed peer as a new configuration entry and the follower is observed again.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the restarted follower is reconnected to the live leader in both directions.

The restarted follower has no snapshot of its own (snapshot_count 0) and its log already matches the leader's for every entry the leader holds, so no snapshot is shipped and no configuration entry is newly appended before the observation.
The leader stays live and healthy throughout, is in Leader state when the follower is observed, and the new configuration entry is appended by that same leader afterwards.
The observation and repair windows are 400 ms each; the follower's last log index and last applied index are emitted as operands.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, restarts of more than one member, membership changes between the two observation points other than the single re-add, and any claim about the follower's behaviour while no leader is reachable.

scope.description: Whether a restarted instance whose reconstruction is empty still enforces the committed configuration's voter gate when it decides whether to grant support. Thirteen in-process cases: the eleven previously exercised restart shapes plus a vote_gate_after_restart case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-peer cluster demotes one peer to a nonvoter while it keeps receiving entries, a voter follower is restarted alone, the leader is stopped so the restarted instance knows no leader, and the demoted peer's real transport delivers a real RequestVote to the restarted instance.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the restarted instance is reconnected to the two live peers in both directions.

The request represents the campaign of a peer whose own reconstruction still counts it as a voter, which is the mirror of the defect under audit: it carries that peer's real identity, address and last log entry, and claims a term one above the restarted instance's so that the request is not filtered by the duplicate-vote rule for a term in which the responder already voted during the cluster's initial election.

No responder state is fabricated: the request is delivered over the real transport to the real handler, and the responder's configuration, term and persisted vote are read back from its own memory and stable store.
Both peers hold the same last log entry, so the log up-to-dateness checks do not by themselves decide the request; the observation window after stopping the leader is 200 ms.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, pre-vote delivery, campaigns started by the target instance itself, and any claim about votes cast by peers other than the one delivering the request.

basis.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes one non-leader peer to a nonvoter, applies 20 entries so both peers hold the same log, reads the responder's own configuration entry, voter count and snapshot count, stops only the responder and emits a vote_inputs CA_EVENT, then rebuilds the responder over its own stores and reconnects it in both directions to the two live peers. It then emits a vote_grant CA_EVENT with the responder's reconstructed voter count, its log's voter count, the granted flag, the response term, the responder's terms before and after, the candidate's membership and vote status in the committed configuration, and the vote term and candidate persisted in the responder's stable store before and after the request.

result.summary: Built and registered the execution for the strongest remaining boundary, a partition between the two configurations. The successor experiment's new split_configurations case collapses a three-voter committed configuration to one voter, snapshots it, makes it three voters again, disconnects the leader from the other two in both directions before stopping it, restarts only the leader with a fresh instance beside it, and then lets both sides elect and commit. Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled both sides elected leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums — the restarted side on its one-voter reconstruction, the two peers on the committed three-voter configuration — both sides committed a uniquely named entry and neither side's store held the other's entry; with the flag disabled only the two-peer side led and the restarted side refused with "node is not the leader". Four comparisons are declared: both sides leading and both holding the same term for the flag-enabled case (each predicted violated), cross-side visibility of the two committed entries (also predicted violated), and the flag-disabled control (predicted to hold). Validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so no interpretation was recorded and the split-configuration consequence is not yet part of the account; the harness addition is the turn's substantive work.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: four in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities, pairing RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled within two single-voter committed shapes. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, optionally snapshots and then commits RemoveServer for the non-leader peer, reads the configuration entry and tracked commit index from the surviving instance's own log store, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same log, stable and snapshot stores plus a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In both shapes the committed configuration after the setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration (1 voter) with no snapshot, or a snapshot taken before a committed RemoveServer that leaves 1 voter while the snapshot metadata still holds 2.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms) and the flag-disabled control runs the identical setup for each shape.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

basis.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands through the elected leader, and for the second shape calls leader.Snapshot() followed by leader.RemoveServer(non-leader ID) plus 10 more applies. Before the restart it reads, from the surviving instance's own stores, the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list) together with the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it then shuts down every instance and restarts the survivor with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote. Each emitted CA_EVENT JSON line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity, plus raw operands (latest_config_index, log_config_index, snapshot_config_index and the server lists), the instance's own configuration, the public GetConfiguration view, last_applied, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix, election attempts and became_leader over the 3000 ms window.

scope.description: Whether a reconstructed configuration smaller than the committed one changes which support counts. Seven in-process cases: the five previously exercised restart shapes (no-snapshot, snapshot-then-RemoveServer, and the within-flag case whose configuration entry stays above the replayed prefix) plus a new shape in which the snapshot records one voter because the second peer was demoted before it and the committed configuration afterwards has two voters because the peer was promoted again after it; that shape runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In the new shape, after the bounded leadership wait the other instance is stopped and one entry is committed with a 1000 ms Apply timeout, so the support the completed decision rested on is observable.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no membership change is issued after it.
In the new shape the committed configuration has two voters after the promotion while the node's own snapshot metadata still carries the demoted configuration with a single voter.

Every instance of the cluster is stopped before the restart in each case, so after the restart the other member is unavailable in the new shape as well and the surviving instance is the only member of the committed configuration that is running.
The bounded leadership window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms) and the commit attempt uses a 1000 ms Apply timeout.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, restarting more than one member, and post-restart membership changes or snapshot installs.

scope.description: Whether a client membership change issued to a node whose configuration is the reconstructed one commits with support that is not a majority of the configuration it replaces, and whether the peers it demotes adopt it. basis.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back, applies ten more entries and reads the last configuration entry into a split_inputs CA_EVENT. It disconnects the leader from both peers in both directions with the transport's Disconnect, stops the leader, restarts it over its own stores with the case flag, starts one fresh empty instance (own stores and FSM) connected only to it, and waits for it to lead. It then issues AddVoter for the fresh instance, waits for a leader among the two partitioned peers, records both sides' terms and reconstructed voter counts, has both sides commit a uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, waits, searches each side's log store for the other side's entry, and emits a split_result CA_EVENT with both sides' leadership, terms, voter counts, commit outcomes, whether each side holds its own and the other's entry, the derived cross_entries_seen and whether both sides lead and in the same term.
basis.responsibility: Election quorums and leader commitments are computed from each node's own reconstructed configuration, so whether two quorums overlap is decided by that configuration rather than by the committed one.

comparisons.description: Partition case with the flag enabled: a cluster is not expected to have a leader on the restarted side and a leader among the peers of the committed configuration at the same time.
Partition case with the flag enabled: two leaders are not expected to hold the same term.
Partition case with the flag enabled: an entry committed on one side is expected to be visible to the other side's store, so both committed entries should be found across the two sides.
Control: with the flag disabled the restarted side cannot lead with only one of the committed configuration's three voters reachable, so only the other side leads.

before.description: Whether a client membership change issued to a node whose configuration is the reconstructed one commits with support that is not a majority of the configuration it replaces, and whether the peers it demotes adopt it. Nineteen in-process cases: the seventeen previously exercised restart shapes plus a client_change_on_reconstruction case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, every instance is stopped, and only the former leader is restarted together with a fresh empty fourth instance; a client AddVoter for that instance is issued with prevIndex 0, and the two demoted peers are then restarted with the flag disabled.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the fresh instance has its own empty log, stable and snapshot stores and is connected to the restarted leader in both directions, and the returning peers are reconnected likewise.
The two peers of the committed configuration are deliberately kept down while the change is issued, so the leader cannot reach them and any commit must rest on itself and the fresh instance.
The client change is the package's own AddVoter with prevIndex 0, as the package's AddPeer and RemovePeer helpers also use.

The change wait is 400 ms and the observation of the returning peers a further 400 ms; the returning peers are restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so their own configuration comes from their logs.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, membership changes with a nonzero prevIndex, concurrent client changes, and any claim about leadership among disjoint configurations after a partition.

after.description: Whether a reconstruction-governed leader and the peers of the committed configuration can both lead and commit when a partition separates them. Twenty-one in-process cases: the nineteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a split_configurations case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, the leader is disconnected from the other two in both directions and stopped, only it is restarted together with a fresh empty instance, and both sides are left to elect and commit.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the partition is made with the transport's own Disconnect on both sides, and the fresh instance is connected only to the restarted leader.

The restarted leader's reconstruction is the single-voter configuration recorded by its own snapshot while the configuration entry in its log names three voters; the two partitioned peers keep the committed configuration.
Each side is given up to 800 ms to elect, then both are asked to commit one uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, and each side's log store is searched for the other side's entry afterwards.
No instance is restarted after the partition, and no other membership change is issued on the second side.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, healing of the partition, multiple sequential client changes, and any claim about what the cluster would do if the partition were repaired.

prefix.before: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back and applies ten more entries, reads the last configuration entry and emits a change_inputs CA_EVENT, then shuts down every instance.
